key_insight: PyraTok learns discrete video tokens at multiple spatiotemporal scales and explicitly aligns them with language, producing semantically structured representations that improve cross-modal alignment and zero-shot transfer.
problem_solved: Existing video tokenizers use single-scale codebooks with limited vocabularies and weak language supervision, leading to poor semantic alignment with text and limited zero-shot capability for video understanding and generation.
method: Construct a pyramidal tokenizer on top of a pretrained video VAE to produce discrete latents at multiple spatiotemporal resolutions (a multi-scale codebook pyramid).
Introduce stronger language alignment across scales so tokens become semantically structured and directly comparable to text representations.
Replace single-scale discrete latents with the language-aligned pyramidal tokens for downstream text-to-video generation and zero-shot video understanding.
impact: PyraTok provides more expressive, language-grounded video tokens that improve cross-modal transfer and reduce reliance on task-specific fine-tuning, benefiting practitioners building text-to-video models, retrieval systems, and zero-shot video classifiers.
visual_elements: Pyramid diagram showing multiple spatiotemporal scales (fine → coarse) with discrete tokens at each level.
Schematic of token-to-text alignment (arrows or heatmap) illustrating improved semantic correspondence between video tokens and language.
Before/after comparison: single-scale tokenizer vs PyraTok on a sample generation or retrieval example.
Bar chart or radar plot summarizing gains in cross-modal alignment and zero-shot transfer (conceptual, not necessarily numeric).
paper_title: PyraTok: Language-Aligned Pyramidal Tokenizer for Video Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Adheesh Juvekar, Kiet A. Nguyen, Dong-Hwan Jang
